details: A single flow-matching image generator is expected to support text-to-image (T2I), local editing, and global editing, but jointly training these capabilities causes interference, while data mixing, weight merging, and inference-time score composition yield compromise solutions.

Framing capability composition as querying frozen capability velocity fields exposes three coupled failure modes: target-field ambiguity (which field supervises a sample), state-distribution mismatch (where the field is queried), and trajectory-query correlation (how many rollout states are used).

DanceOPD: on-policy generative field distillation, where each frozen capability source (T2I model, edit model, realism model, or an operator such as classifier-free guidance) is treated as a velocity field over a shared flow state space.

Each training step hard-routes a sample to exactly one capability field (preserving its semantic identity), queries that field at a single stop-gradient state drawn from the current student's own rollout, biased toward the low-noise/semantic side, and updates the student with plain velocity MSE.
Justification: under a local equal-covariance Gaussian transition view, KL-style field matching reduces to a (weighted) velocity MSE, so direct velocity regression is the natural local objective.
Main backbone Z-Image; student trained as DiT LoRA (rank 128), AdamW, lr 2e-4, grad accumulation 4.
Capability teachers built from OmniEdit fine-tuning: attribute subsets = local-edit field, style subsets = global-edit field, full data = joint edit field; base Z-Image = T2I field.

Default query recipe: 16-step Euler ODE stop-gradient student rollout, K=1 query per sample, semantic coordinate s~Beta(5,2) (low-t bias), uniform route probabilities (1:1 for two-bucket composition, 1:1:1 for three-bucket diagnostics); student initialized from the attribute-edit SFT LoRA.
Realism-field absorption uses SD3.5-M; realism teacher trained full-parameter for 100k steps (lr 1e-5, bs 16), with OPD/distillation runs reported up to 3k steps.

Four settings: T2I + edit composition; local + global edit composition; realism-field absorption with T2I preservation; classifier-free-guidance absorption (target field with train scale alpha, eval scale beta, effective ~alpha*beta).
GEditBench-EN, averaged over six categories (subject addition/replacement/removal, background change, style change, color alteration), 28 sampling steps, CFG 7.0.
GenEval overall plus per-category, 28 steps, CFG 3.5, used as the anchor-capability preservation measure.
Realism: proprietary photorealism reward model on 200 held-out prompts at 1024x1024, 28 steps, CFG 3.5.
Off-policy distillation: identical hard routing and MSE but query states from forward-noised offline endpoints instead of student rollout.
DiffusionOPD reproduction (not open-sourced): on-policy ODE rollout with dense full-trajectory transition-mean matching, K=16, plus same-step multi-bucket accumulation.
Flow-OPD reproduction (official code adapted): SDE rollout with cached log-probs, teacher transition-KL reward, PPO-style clipping, group size 16, MAR disabled.
Joint/mixed training and weight-merging composition baselines.
Routing x objective 2x2: hard routing vs soft all-teacher mixing, under MSE vs KL-sigma^2 weighting.
Aggregation: step alternation vs same-step accumulation over G=3 buckets, with K=1 and K=2; SDE rollout injected as a decorrelation control.
Query design: low-t vs median-t vs high-t Beta distributions; K=1 vs weighted dense K=2,4,8,16; rollout lengths 8/16/20/28 steps.
Objectives: timestep(Min-SNR)-weighted MSE, KL-sigma^2, DMD-EMA hybrid, pure DMD, SDS+DMD, DMD2-inter/dist, consistency-style, auxiliary hidden-feature distillation.
Initialization: local-edit vs merged vs global-edit vs T2I checkpoint; per-step wall-clock cost decomposition (rollout cost N*C_roll plus K gradient-bearing queries).

key_findings.finding: Hard-routed, single-query on-policy field matching composes heterogeneous capabilities without the usual anchor degradation, in some cases exceeding the individual source models.
key_findings.evidence: In T2I+edit composition, GEditBench average rises 8.1% over the best reproduced OPD baseline and 8.5% over the edit source, while GenEval overall rises 2.0% over the T2I source and 1.6% over the strongest composition baseline; largest edit gains over DiffusionOPD are background change +21.9% and style change +21.3%. In local+global edit composition, GEditBench improves 16.1% over the best competing composition baseline and 7.9% over the local-edit source, with GenEval +2.5%, concentrated in background change (+33.5%), style change (+12.9%), and color alteration (+11.6%).

key_findings.finding: A single low-noise semantic-side query per rollout is both cheaper and better than dense or higher-noise trajectory querying, because within-rollout states supply correlated supervision.
key_findings.evidence: Low-t querying beats median-t and high-t by 23.7% and 19.5% on GEditBench average (e.g. +46.1% subject addition and +57.1% style change vs high-t); K=1 beats weighted dense variants at K=2,4,8,16 by 16.6%, 7.9%, 10.2%, and 12.2%. In the dense stress case (K=2, G=3, -22.8% vs default), replacing ODE with SDE rollout recovers 18.4% but remains 8.6% below the single-query default, and SDE hurts the control settings by 15.3% and 8.3%; a variance identity Var = sigma^2/K (1+(K-1)rho) formalizes why correlated queries do not add information.

key_findings.finding: Target-field construction, not the matching objective, is the dominant factor: averaging several teacher fields inside one sample destroys its capability identity, and conflict also reappears at the optimizer-step level.
key_findings.evidence: Hard routing beats soft all-teacher mixing by 15.2% under MSE and 10.6% under KL-sigma^2 (largest gains: background change +20.8%, subject removal +26.8% under MSE), while same-step accumulation of G=3 routed buckets still loses 4.6% on average (subject addition -17.5%, subject removal -13.5%) despite every sample keeping a valid routed target; appendix derives the mixture bias sum_{m != y} w_m (v_m - v_y).

key_findings.finding: Querying on student-visited states rather than offline noised states substantially improves absorption of a non-task field (realism) at no cost to base generation.
key_findings.evidence: On SD3.5-M, DanceOPD raises the realism reward 9.9% over off-policy distillation and closes 85.3% of the student-to-teacher reward gap, while its T2I score stays within 0.1% of off-policy distillation and is 7.6% above the student anchor; qualitatively it sharpens texture/lighting where off-policy distillation shows washed-out or over-saturated structure.

key_findings.finding: Classifier-free guidance can be absorbed as an ordinary capability field, but absorbed and inference-time guidance compose multiplicatively, so the standard evaluation convention over-guides the student.
key_findings.evidence: With effective scale approximately alpha*beta, the best measured composition improves GEditBench average by 7.6% over train-only absorption (alpha=3.5, beta=1) and 1.4% over eval-only CFG (alpha=1, beta=7), with gains of 10.3-22.5% on subject replacement, background change, color alteration and subject removal, whereas over-guided composition drops 31.2% relative to the best setting.
